---
title: "`ev_enrich()` — ranked GSEA & ORA"
---

## Purpose

Run pathway enrichment for one or more contrasts against the registered
databases, returning a tidy tibble of pathways with NES, p-value, FDR, size and
leading edge.

## When to use

The enrichment stage of the pipeline. Call it directly when you want the
enrichment table without plotting, or to inspect results before
`ev_collapse()`.

## How it works

- **fgsea** (`enrich_mode = "fgsea"`): ranks genes by a **signed** statistic and
  runs `fgsea::fgseaMultilevel` (exact, `eps = 0`). The default rank is the
  limma/proteoDA **moderated t** (`rank_by = "t"`), falling back to
  `sign(logFC)·−log10(p)` when no `t` column exists.
- **ORA** (`enrich_mode = "ora"`): hypergeometric test of significant genes
  against a background (default = all tested genes).

Duplicate gene symbols are reduced to the most extreme signed value before
ranking. Up/down pathways are distinguished by NES sign.

## Parameters & defaults

| Argument | Default | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `rank_by` | `"t"` | moderated t = recommended signed GSEA statistic (Subramanian 2005; Reimand 2019); falls back to `signed_p` |
| `enrich_mode` | `c("fgsea","ora")` | ranked GSEA by default; ORA available |
| `min_size`, `max_size` | `15`, `500` | Reimand 2019 §S3.4: <15 noise-prone, >500 non-specific |
| `nperm` | `10000` | fgsea multilevel precision |
| `exclude_terms` | `"DISEASE\|CANCER\|TUMOR"` | drop disease sets irrelevant to most designs |
| `seed` | `42` | reproducible permutations |

## Literature

- Subramanian A, *et al.* "GSEA." *PNAS* 2005;102(43):15545–50. PMID:16199517.
- Korotkevich G, *et al.* "Fast gene set enrichment analysis." bioRxiv 2021.
  doi:10.1101/060012.
- Reimand J, *et al.* *Nat Protoc* 2019;14:482–517. PMID:30664679.

## Example

```r
e <- ev_enrich(dep, contrast = "CTLvMITO",
               databases = c("hallmark", "reactome", "kegg_legacy"),
               species = "rat", enrich_mode = "fgsea")   # ranks by moderated t
```
